headline: A Stray Source Map Set 512,000 Lines of Claude Code Free
lede: On March 31, 2026, a security researcher noticed a 59.8-megabyte source-map file bundled inside version 2.1.88 of Anthropic's Claude Code npm package — a file that pointed directly to a ZIP archive of roughly 512,000 lines of the company's internal TypeScript source, hosted openly on Cloudflare's infrastructure. Within hours a project called OpenClaude appeared on GitHub, stripping out the Anthropic API dependency and wiring in a compatibility shim that routes Claude Code's full agent machinery to any of 200-plus third-party models. The episode exposed an unusually candid cross-section of a commercially sensitive product and set off a DMCA sweep that accidentally erased thousands of the wrong repositories.
body:
The root cause was a compound failure. **Bun** — the JavaScript runtime Anthropic uses to build Claude Code — has a confirmed bug (filed as issue *oven-sh/bun#28001*) that causes it to emit *source maps* in production builds even when the configuration says otherwise. Source maps are developer-facing files that reconstitute minified JavaScript back into the original source code; bundled accidentally into a published package, they expose a full codebase as thoroughly as handing over the repository. Compounding the bug, the npm package lacked a `.npmignore` entry to strip map files before publication, and no pre-publish check caught the artifact. The map file pointed to a ZIP archive of roughly 1,900 TypeScript files on a public Cloudflare (NET) R2 storage bucket. Anthropic pulled version 2.1.88 the same day and described the incident as “a release packaging issue caused by human error, not a security breach.” No customer data or model weights were involved.

The leaked code offered an unusually candid look at a fast-growing *agentic coding tool*. Internal comments documented a feature called Undercover Mode that strips Claude’s attribution headers and blocks the use of internal project codenames in commits to external repositories. The codebase also contained tooling labelled *anti-distillation*: fake tool definitions injected into model prompts, apparently designed to degrade competitors’ training data if they attempted to scrape Claude Code interactions, gated behind a feature flag. A background daemon called KAIROS, referenced more than 150 times but apparently never shipped to users, was designed to run on 15-second decision cycles and monitor GitHub webhooks autonomously. An internal benchmark cited in the code put the latest model’s false-claims rate at 29–30%.

GitHub user mjohnnywest published **OpenClaude** within roughly 24 hours of researcher Chaofan Shou’s public disclosure. The project preserves Claude Code’s full toolkit — Bash execution, file operations, web search, *MCP* integrations, multi-agent orchestration — while replacing the Anthropic API backend with a translation shim of roughly 724 lines that maps Anthropic’s proprietary message format to the *OpenAI Chat Completions API* standard. The “200+” figure refers chiefly to OpenRouter, a unified inference aggregator that speaks the same standard and catalogs more than 200 models under a single endpoint; the screenshot in the original post shows the tool already running against z-ai/glm5 via an NVIDIA (NVDA) inference endpoint — a working demonstration of the portability claim. The README acknowledges that the original source remains subject to Anthropic’s terms while claiming the shim additions are public domain, a legal distinction whose durability is untested.

Anthropic’s initial DMCA notice, filed March 31, targeted one parent repository and roughly 8,100 forks in its network. The sweep accidentally ensnared forks of Anthropic’s own separate public Claude Code repository — a legally distinct codebase — prompting a retraction filed the following day that narrowed enforcement to one repository and 96 specific forks. Anthropic’s head of Claude Code acknowledged the overbreadth was unintentional. Multiple OpenClaude mirrors, described by their maintainers as intentionally irremovable, remained live; their legal status is contested. Anthropic issued no formal technical post-mortem and quietly deprecated npm as a Claude Code installation method in its official documentation.

concepts.definition: A file that maps compiled or minified JavaScript back to the original source code, allowing developers to debug production builds as if they were reading unprocessed code. When accidentally included in a published npm package, a source map can expose the full original codebase to anyone who downloads the package.

The Node Package Manager, the dominant registry and command-line tool for distributing JavaScript libraries and applications. Developers publish packages to npm and install them as dependencies; a published package is publicly downloadable by default.

Software that autonomously reads, writes, and executes code on a developer’s behalf, taking multi-step actions — running tests, editing files, querying APIs — without requiring explicit instruction for each step. Claude Code is an example: it reasons about a task and acts rather than just answering questions.

A widely adopted API standard, originated by OpenAI, for sending messages to a language model and receiving a structured response. Many providers now implement the same interface, making it a de facto interoperability standard: a client built for one model can switch to another by changing a single endpoint URL.

The Digital Millennium Copyright Act, a U.S. law that lets copyright holders request online platforms remove infringing content via a takedown notice. Platforms like GitHub must comply quickly or risk losing their safe-harbor liability protections; recipients can file counter-notices to contest a removal.

An open protocol that lets AI assistants connect to external tools and data sources through a standardized interface. Claude Code uses MCP integrations to communicate with third-party services without requiring custom per-service code.

A technique in which a model provider injects deliberately false or misleading information into model prompts to corrupt the training data of any competitor attempting to distill a smaller model from observed interactions. The goal is to make scraped outputs unreliable for training rival systems.

repos.summary: OpenClaude is a fork of the Claude Code source accidentally exposed via an npm source map in March 2026. It replaces Anthropic’s proprietary API backend with a shim that translates Anthropic’s message format to the OpenAI Chat Completions API standard, preserving all of Claude Code’s built-in tools. The project lets developers run Claude Code’s full agent machinery against any model available through OpenRouter, Ollama, or any other OpenAI-compatible provider.

fact_check: OpenClaude’s own UI advertises “Zero limits,” which is misleading: rate limits, per-token costs, and content policies all apply, inherited from whatever backend provider the user configures. The “200+” model figure is accurate for OpenRouter but describes models available via that aggregator, not models OpenClaude itself bundles or validates. Whether the shim’s “public domain” claim insulates it from Anthropic’s copyright over the original Claude Code source has not been adjudicated.
